questions.evidence:
At a school book fair, the visiting bookshop gives Hugo a coupon for twenty dollars off a future purchase of at least two hundred dollars. The coupon starts tomorrow and expires at the end of the month. It cannot be used with another coupon, and it gives no cash change.

Hugo's current books cost one hundred and eighty dollars. He considers adding a thirty-dollar notebook to reach the minimum and use the coupon now. The cashier points to the starting date. Buying an extra item today would not make the coupon valid earlier.

Hugo pays for the books he needs and keeps the coupon separately. The next week, he plans to buy a dictionary priced at two hundred and twenty dollars. Before relying on the discount, he checks that the date falls inside the coupon period and that the dictionary is eligible.

He spends two hundred dollars on the dictionary after the discount. The extra notebook was never needed. Hugo learns that a threshold and a valid date are separate conditions; meeting one does not automatically satisfy the other.
